chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, moderation is a matter which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves, and indeed, extravagance is a matter which Allah hates, to the extent of your throwing the date-stone, for it is suitable for something, and to your pouring out the remainder of your drink.

key_terms.النَّوَاةَ: The stone or pit of a fruit (e.g., date), often discarded but still useful
key_terms.الْقَصْدَ: Moderation or balance in consumption and conduct
key_terms.فَضْلَ شَرَابِكَ: The remainder or surplus of one's drink

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about wasting small amounts of food or drink?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines moderation as a divine virtue and extravagance as a beloved vice, using the vivid examples of discarding a date stone or spilling drink to illustrate that waste extends beyond mere excess to the neglect of utility. This teaching aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *israf* (extravagance) as a spiritual and physical corruption, reinforcing the concept that every blessing, no matter how small, holds value in the eyes of Allah. It serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate gratitude and mindfulness in their daily consumption habits.
